source_evidence.example_warning: All examples and stand-in replies in this preparation are synthetic schema fixtures, not observed provider responses.

design.selected: One pending status batch owned by the existing Codex worker, returned as a correlated invoke result.
design.alternative_rejected: A generic session response multiplexer duplicates existing buffering and expands transport ownership. Existing call and interrupt already preserve nonmatching replies for next_event.
design.caller: codex_mcp_status(chat_id) obtains an existing runner, enqueues a query, drops its temporary Arc and waits with an absolute deadline.
design.worker_state: Idle or Pending { current_request_id, accumulated_rows, seen_cursors, deadline, result_sender }, scoped to exactly one live process.
design.lifecycle: Fail and remove Pending on close, shutdown, session replacement, write failure and interrupt Closed/Io. Late replies do not satisfy a new process or request.
design.deadline: Timestamp before command enqueue; one deadline across waiting, pagination and receiver delivery. Recheck Instant after receiver returns, even for an already queued success at zero remaining timeout. Never emit expired rows even if a blocking existing operation buffered them earlier.
design.frontend: A result-driven local dialog with idle/loading/success/error state and request-generation invalidation on close/chat/provider change. Only Codex is enabled in this unit. No rows derived from configuration, tools executed in a turn, Reason org connections or simulated status.

strict_decoding.normalization: connected iff serverInfo is non-null or at least one actual tool exists; otherwise needs-auth iff notLoggedIn, else failed. Emit name, status, tools; do not forward serverInfo.

fixture_review.bootstrap: hold-until-turn completes the first turn before awaiting another start; otherwise the runner would keep the next prompt queued forever.
fixture_review.deadline_proof: buffered-expired emits the status reply during interrupt and delays its own interrupt response across the deadline. A separate direct receiver test must prove rejection of an already-queued result after deadline; the subprocess alone cannot prove receiver delivery semantics.
fixture_review.lifecycle_proof: close, interrupt-close and broken-stdin are distinct subprocess fixtures. Runner shutdown/replacement/session-drop and approval/consent/default-answer write-failure assertions must also target the actual production paths, not merely use stdout closure as their proxy.
fixture_review.fixture_scope: The script validates MCP request IDs/params, resets its expected cursor after intentionally malformed/repeated pages so retries start a fresh batch, rejects premature interrupts before a delayed turn/started notification, and provides schema variants and consent/approval requests. It is preparation, not a complete regression test suite. All scenarios still require actual assertions and RED/GREEN execution.

planned_behavior_cases.case: An unstarted/closed chat query fails without launching a process or emitting a user turn.
The first real query writes mcpServerStatus/list with empty params and a unique shared request ID.
All pages are accumulated; only nonterminal cursors are sent, and null or empty string stops pagination.
Valid empty data yields an empty successful result, never a fabricated server.
Non-null server information or an actual tool marks connected; empty notLoggedIn marks needs-auth; all other empty auth states mark failed.
Optional tool description and readOnly/destructive/openWorld annotations survive normalization; null optional values are rejected.
Missing required-nullable fields, null tool values, unknown auth states and malformed rows/pages reject the query.
An RPC error is returned as a query error, not a failed server row or TurnEnded.
A wrong response ID cannot complete a pending query; a matching success or error can.
A second overlapping query is bounded/rejected without corrupting the first batch.
A status response arriving during an existing start_turn call is preserved and resolved afterward; turn notifications remain ordered.
A status response arriving during interrupt is preserved; Stop and permission/consent replies continue through the normal owner.
Queue delay, pagination delay, a late buffered response and an already-queued result received after deadline cannot produce success; repeated cursors reject. Recheck deadline after receiver delivery.
Process close, shutdown, replacement, write failure and interrupt Closed/Io fail pending status; restart cannot adopt old replies.

The actual Composer action deletes only a validated unshadowed MCP slash range, opens a result-driven Codex dialog and ignores stale completions; collisions, suffixes, attachments and IME/range guards remain unchanged.
